A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Gaussian-splatting point-cloud completion work, despite v2's new ComPC title and substantial revisions. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. V1 ends with references; v2 includes accessible appendix Sections A.1–A.10.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic and Redwood completion results in Tables 1–2 and qualitative component ablations in Figures 7–11.

after.justification: V2 reports updated completion experiments, quantitative ablations, and original appendix evaluations covering robustness, multiple completions, ShapeNet, meshes, and LiDAR scans.

M1.justification: V1 optimizes reference-image colors and Gaussian scaling using depth-conditioned ControlNet SDS. V2 replaces this stage with fixed colors derived from estimated surface normals, removing that diffusion optimization stage (Section 3.1). The core Zero-1-to-3 completion machinery remains. Point Cloud Extraction mostly reorganizes existing surface extraction and Grid Pulling; Appendix A.8 additionally uses Marching Cubes to produce meshes.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained synthetic objects and Redwood scans, v2 evaluates ShapeNet chair, table, pistol, and tower objects and KITTI LiDAR pedestrian, cyclist, car, and truck scans (A.9–A.10). It also introduces noisy inputs, deliberately missing center/edge regions, and varying observation completeness (A.5–A.6), substantially expanding evaluated conditions.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 remove Snowflake and add PointAttN, ShapeFormer, and SVDFormer while retaining PoinTr, SeedFormer, and AdaPoinTr. Table 2 adds a direct SDS-Complete comparison, absent from v1's experiments despite its discussion there. The qualitative comparator sets also change: Figures 5–6 drop SeedFormer and Snowflake and introduce newer methods.

E3.justification: V2 introduces controlled noise levels, partial inputs assembled from 1, 3, or 7 depth maps, and evaluation using TMD/UHD/MMD (A.5–A.7). Table 2 specifies reoptimization and consistent normalization for the newly evaluated SDS-Complete baseline. These substantially extend evaluation design; the retained main comparisons still use CD/EMD and 16,384 points.

E4.justification: The ControlNet-versus-depth ablation becomes a depth/coordinate/normal colorization comparison with quantitative evidence (Figure 7, Table 3). Existing component, Grid Pulling, Gaussian-modification, and fractal ablations gain quantitative results in Tables 4 and 6–8; their relocation alone is not an addition. New analyses examine thin-surface failures, missing reference regions, noise, incompleteness, and completion diversity.

E5.justification: V1 gives no repeated-run information. V2 states that its main synthetic and real-scan results average three experiments and that the multimodal comparison uses four optimizations per method (Section 4; A.7). These are newly reported practices, not a documented increase from a known v1 run count. No confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the proposed method's reported average CD/EMD of 1.75/2.33 with 1.43/1.88. Table 2 replaces its in-domain average of 1.57/2.52 with 1.35/2.03 and out-of-domain average of 2.58/3.25 with 2.57/3.17. These accompany method and reporting changes, so they do not isolate the revision's effect. V2 also adds extensive comparator, ablation, robustness, ShapeNet, and multimodal results; Table 11 reports better average UHD/MMD but lower diversity than SDS-Complete.

T1.justification: Mathematical changes concern method specification: the ControlNet colorization objectives disappear, a normal-based color definition is introduced, and the final-output expression is revised from merging g(Ps) to merging explicitly pulled 3D points (v1 Section 3.2; v2 Section 3.3). Most remaining equations are retained with renumbering. Neither version presents theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claim of prompt-free completion across unseen categories using 2D priors remains. The abstract and contribution list replace learned colorization with Partial Gaussian Initialization and elevate extraction to a separate contribution. V2's conclusion explicitly extends its superiority claim to test-time approaches as well as network-based methods.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the texture-based colorization explanation with an argument about normals revealing surface geometry. It adds the CD-versus-EMD tradeoff from Grid Pulling, thin-surface failure explanations, limits under missing observations and noise, and known-category ShapeNet qualifications. Appendix A.7 also newly interprets reduced diversity as convergence toward ground truth. These substantially expand the paper's mechanisms and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: V2 newly supplies numerical loss weights, noise parameters, 1,000 ZFC and 5,000 PCE iterations, GPU/software versions, and approximate runtime (Table 5; A.1; Section 5). It specifies Open3D normal estimation, Gaussian scale initialization, and 500 surface-extraction viewpoints, and adds a project-page address. These fill substantial documentation gaps; the newly disclosed budgets do not establish changes from v1's unspecified budgets.

R1.justification: V2 adds recent completion and diffusion references, including PointAttN, SVDFormer, ShapeFormer, and DiffComplete, while removing several 3D-native generation references. It changes SDS-Complete's described renderer and citation from NeuS to VolSDF and makes the efficiency contrast explicit. The central positioning around prompt-free completion using pretrained 2D priors remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and method narrative are substantially revised around ComPC and a three-stage organization. Extraction receives its own subsection, several main-text ablations move into the new appendix, and limitations precede the conclusion. Expanded background explanations and revised terminology produce substantial editorial and structural changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the pipeline in Figure 2, revises qualitative comparison panels and ablation labels, expands Tables 1–2, and adds Tables 3–12 and Figures 12–18. Earlier ablation figures are retained and relocated into the appendix. The conference template also changes typography, headers, text width, and placement throughout.

improvement.justification: V2 resolves important validation gaps by directly comparing with SDS-Complete and quantifying component effects that v1 only illustrated. Corruption tests, additional datasets and sensor types, and explicit failure cases make the generalization claims substantially more assessable; implementation settings improve reproducibility. LiDAR evidence remains qualitative, and A.7's favorable interpretation of reduced diversity is weakly supported, but these limitations do not outweigh the stronger validation and documentation. This judgment does not depend on treating updated scores as isolated performance gains.
